thread:
sofia: FYI I'm hitting a reproducible UX freeze in the sampleapp onboarding flow. When token rotation happens mid-pagination the SDK seems to slam the client concurrency window down and the paginator backs up. Not seeing upstream 429s, but users see a 5-8s pause. Anyone run into this pattern?

aaron: is this the new adaptive-window paginator we shipped last month?

sofia: yes. repro steps: start 6 parallel clients, each scanning with pageSize=40, force token refresh ~6s after start. After refresh we observe per-client window go from ~8 to 1, then lots of queued fetchPage calls.

sofia: example log snippet (condensed):
[2026-03-21T09:41:10Z] fetchPage(c=2,p=7) -> 200 latency=95ms
[2026-03-21T09:41:16Z] auth:refresh(c=2) -> 200
[2026-03-21T09:41:16Z] window.adjust(c=2) old=8 new=1 reason=auth_event
[2026-03-21T09:41:16Z] enqueue(c=4,p=9) queued=5 wait=4.1s

jin: dropping to 1 on any auth_event sounds like a safety clamp that is too aggressive. We probably intended to protect against cascading errors, but it creates a backpressure feedback loop with prefetch.

leo: agree. The sequence is: clamp -> prefetch buffer drains -> paginator tries to refill aggressively -> those requests queue behind clamp -> visible stall. That's a control-feedback oscillation.

aaron: two quick fixes: (1) on auth_event success (2xx) don't clamp below min(ceil(old*0.25), 2). (2) make prefetch target scale with current window so we don't over-request when window shrinks.

jin: +1 to both. Also add a fast-path: if token refresh returned 2xx and the next N downstream requests have <3% error rate, ramp back up faster instead of waiting long decay.

ops-bot: Note created: TICKET-8897 "sdk: avoid single-slot clamp on auth refresh to prevent prefetch stalls" with logs attached.

sofia: can we add a deterministic CI test? plan: simulate token TTL edge and 6 clients, assert no client experiences >3s average queue time during rotation. I can prototype a test harness that manipulates clock and token TTL.

leo: also add a short doc blurb in devex onboarding: "token rotation can interact with client-side backpressure; for heavy pagination set refresh margin >30s or use long-lived tokens during onboarding load tests."

jin: I'll submit a small patch that changes the clamp heuristic and ties prefetch target to window. I'll include comments and an env var toggle like SDK_PREFETCH_WINDOW_SCALE for experiments.

aaron: great. once the patch is up let's run the sampleapp load generator (https://ci.internal/redwood/sampleapp-load) and watch the per-client wait histogram in the console. If we still see >3s spikes we can further relax the clamp or add a short grace window post-refresh.

sofia: thanks all, I'll open the test PR and link it here. :rocket:
